commit_reviews.summary: Behavior-preserving repository extraction that centralizes SQL, per-owner scoping, and schema migration logic, leaving routes thin and removing duplicated TASK_SELECT fragments.

compounding_issues: No tests existed after Session 1 (greenfield shipped untested); the first regression safety net only appeared with Session 2's auth feature, so the initial refactors in S1 had no coverage to catch regressions

The owner_id schema migration (ALTER TABLE for legacy DBs) was bolted onto app.py in Session 2 and had to be carried verbatim into the repository layer in Session 4, coupling a one-time migration concern to the refactored data layer
Build artifacts were committed in Sessions 4 and 5 (__pycache__/*.pyc, tasks.db binary), degrading repo hygiene as scope grew

Weak SECRET_KEY default ('change-me-in-production') set in Session 2 was never hardened in later sessions, and SQLite foreign keys (owner_id) are never enabled with PRAGMA foreign_keys, so referential integrity is unenforced
key_decisions: Adopted a single-file raw sqlite3 persistence layer (no ORM) in Session 1 and retained it throughout, keeping the data layer simple and portable
Introduced JWT auth with werkzeug password hashing and per-user owner_id ownership isolation in Session 2, including a backward-compatible ALTER TABLE migration for pre-existing data
Decoupled task-completion notifications onto Celery/Redis in Session 3 with graceful degradation — a broker outage is caught and logged rather than failing the API request
Extracted a repository pattern (BaseRepository ABC, UserRepository, TaskRepository, custom UsernameAlreadyExistsError) in Session 4, slimming app.py and isolating SQL behind named operations
Added JWT-subject-keyed Flask-Limiter rate limiting and id-cursor pagination on list_tasks in Session 5 as the cross-cutting layer on top of the refactored repositories
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across all five sessions. Session 1 delivered a clean but minimal single-file CRUD API with zero tests; Session 2 added the most consequential layer — JWT authentication, per-user ownership isolation, and a data migration — and established the testing discipline that every later session maintained. Session 3 integrated asynchronous Celery notifications with careful failure handling and deduplication tests. Session 4 was a genuine refactor that extracted the repository layer without changing behavior, and all existing tests still passed. Session 5 rounded out production concerns with rate limiting and pagination, again fully tested. The only flat spot is hygiene: build artifacts were committed late and the untested first session set a fragile baseline, but the arc from minimal prototype to a well-structured, multi-user, instrumented service is coherent and mostly upward.
story_review.summary: A coherent five-session arc that progressed logically from a minimal SQLite task API to a tested, multi-user service with auth, async notifications, a repository layer, and cross-cutting rate limiting — with quality improving each session despite an untested start and some committed build artifacts.
